$comment: A debt register, not a suppression list. Every entry is a policy default value the pinned ALZ library declares and the emitted global layer does not yet supply. Test-AlzPolicyDefaults.ps1 prints each one with its reason on every run, fails if a waiver goes stale (the value is now supplied) or is orphaned (the library no longer declares it), and enforces the budget below. The budget only ever goes DOWN: supplying a value means deleting its waiver and decrementing the budget in the same change.

waivers.reason: The factory creates no DDoS Network Protection plan, and one costs roughly USD 2,900/month. The library's own description says to set Enable-DDoS-VNET to DoNotEnforce when the plan is not used. Supplying a fake ID is worse than not supplying one: the policy is a Modify effect, so it would try to write a non-existent plan onto every virtual network at create and update.
waivers.resolution: The wizard's policy selection step decides this: selecting DDoS protection collects a real plan ID, and not selecting it emits creation_enabled = false for Enable-DDoS-VNET.

waivers.reason: Derivable from azure.subscriptions.connectivity, which the config already carries. waivers.resolution: Emit it into the global layer from config.
